newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen edges up on JGBs but sales likely.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen edges up on JGBs but sales likely.

text.p: The key March three-month euroyen futures contract had edged higher by the end of Friday morning trade on stronger Japanese government bond (JGB) futures, but further gains were blocked for now by sales lined up around 99.13, traders said.

Still, sentiment remains positive after Thursday's Bank of Japan (BOJ) quarterly economic report, whose somewhat bearish tone has strengthened market feelings that there will be no change in interest rates for the present, and yet more gains may well lie ahead, they added. The key March contract ended the morning up by 0.03 at 99.12.
Despite the overall firm tone, the March ranged narrowly, from 99.11 to 99.13. Turnover was 36,316 contracts.
"In general, we're seeing a gradual rising trend, with today's low above Thursday's high," said one city bank trader, adding that the next key point to try for would be 99.14.
Although he said sales appeared to be lining up at around 99.13 from both dealers and institutional investors, other traders were not so sure, saying they saw few good reasons to sell right now.
The key September JGB futures contract ended the morning at 126.00, a healthy gain over Thursday's 125.78 close.
